documents.unit: Office of the Provost, Center for Teaching Excellence
documents.title: Generative AI and Pedagogy at SMU
documents.stance_why: The page says 'It is at the discretion of the faculty member whether to use Generative AI in their classroom' while 'SMU requires that faculty communicate to students about the use of AI via their syllabus'; no default rule is set, so the decision is delegated to instructors.
documents.summary: Provost CTE page leaving AI use to faculty discretion but requiring syllabus communication, with a statement builder. Adds tool lists, a Q&A on faculty worries, assignment design and faculty uses of ChatGPT, and data/privacy best practices for prompts.

units.why: Sets the university default as faculty choice: 'It is at the discretion of the faculty member', so the decision is delegated per instructor (P04), addressed to instructors, informing rather than commanding.

units.anchor: SMU requires that faculty communicate to students about the use of AI via their syllabus

units.why: The sentence says faculty 'should provide clear guidelines' covering graded, ungraded and self-study use and other SMU support; an instructor communication expectation (P09), but wider than a syllabus statement.

units.policy: Faculty who use AI in the classroom should provide clear guidelines around AI use in the class for graded and ungraded assignments, self-study outside of class, and support through other SMU avenues.
units.fit_note: Specifies the scope of the guidelines (graded, ungraded, self-study, other SMU support) beyond requiring a syllabus statement.

units.why: Instructors who use AI for 'assignment building or grading' should add 'a disclosure statement'; this is instructor disclosure to students (P47), not student disclosure.

documents.title: Student Guidance (AI)
documents.stance_why: The guide says 'Students should expect every course to include an explicit statement about the use or prohibition of Generative AI' and to 'discuss the parameters with their instructors', so it hands the allow/forbid decision to each course while setting honor-code limits.
documents.summary: OIT student guidance telling students to expect a course AI statement, ask instructors when unsure, and treat AI like help from another person. Includes an Honor Code table of violation and acceptable-use examples per category.

documents.title: Spring 2024: Syllabus Statement Options Regarding the Use of Generative AI
tiers: May be used with appropriate attribution
documents.stance_why: The document is titled 'Syllabus Statement Options' and offers a prohibit statement, a permit-with-attribution statement and a 'Write-in Option', so it is a menu of templates and sets no stance of its own.
documents.summary: Provost template syllabus statements for instructors: one banning generative AI, one permitting it with attribution and student responsibility, and a write-in option. Violations go through the Honor Code.

units.why: The title shows the Provost offers 'Syllabus Statement Options' for instructors to choose from, i.e. named alternative statements (P05).
units.anchor: Syllabus Statement Options Regarding the Use of Generative AI

units.why: The first template says 'Generative AI is not permitted in this course', a default ban on AI in the course (P01).
units.anchor: The use of any form of Generative AI is not permitted in this course.

units.why: Template rationale: assignments are designed so students 'personally develop and demonstrate the knowledge and skills'; AI limited to protect skill-building (P41).
units.anchor: The assignments have been designed to ensure that you personally develop and demonstrate the knowledge

units.why: Students 'are encouraged to maintain clear evidence of your work (e.g., time-stamped drafts and notes)'; keeping drafts (P26), but as proof of ownership, not AI use.
units.anchor: you are encouraged to maintain clear evidence of your work
units.fit_note: Evidence is kept to show ownership of work in a no-AI course, not to log AI use.

units.why: 'Any violation of these rules will be treated... within the SMU Student Honor Code': violations are academic misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: Any violation of these rules will be treated at the undergraduate level within

units.why: 'An incident report will be submitted for review by the Office of Student Conduct and Community Standards' describes the escalation route (P36).
units.anchor: an incident report will be submitted for review by the Office of Student Conduct and
units.fit_note: Describes the reporting procedure, with no penalty stated.

units.why: Second template: 'Generative AI may be used with appropriate attribution', a permit-by-default statement with conditions (P02).
units.anchor: Generative AI may be used with appropriate attribution.

units.why: 'We will cover how Generative AI is used within this discipline, including how to navigate its potential uses and abuses'; teaching AI use as a skill (P44).
units.anchor: In class, we will cover how Generative AI is used within this discipline

units.why: 'Take responsibility for the content' because AI 'can produce content that contains inaccurate information, offensive language/images, and biased' output; students own what they submit (P29).
units.anchor: What you submit is your responsibility across these dimensions.
units.fit_note: Also warns that AI output can be inaccurate, offensive and biased.

units.why: 'Provide clear attribution of your sources' requires AI use be cited with each submission (P24).
units.anchor: Provide clear attribution of your sources.

units.why: Use of AI 'without attribution' 'can be seen as potential academic dishonesty'; nondisclosure is the violation (P28).
units.anchor: Any assignments that utilize Generative AI without attribution
units.fit_note: Anchor is the start of the sentence; the sentence adds that this is treated under the Honor Code.

units.why: The '[Write-in Option: Faculty can choose to create a separate statement regarding AI use here.]' lets each instructor set their own rule (P04).
units.anchor: Faculty can choose to create a separate statement regarding AI use here.
